heros.infro: Wallachian (present-day southern Romania) voivode. Vlad the Impaler is known for the exceedingly cruel punishments he imposed as ruler of Wallachia.
heros.name: vlad tepes

heros.infro: The first wife of King Canuteand mother of Harold I (known as Harefoot), Ælfgifu came from a distinguished English family. She married Canute in 1013, and, although the king later married Emma, Ælfgifu remained a power at court, represented Canute in Norway in 1030, and was probably the force behind Harold during his reign.
heros.name: Alfgifu of Northampton

heros.infro: Imprisoned by his older brother from age 15 to 35, Zara Yaqob was ill-prepared to take over as Emperor of Ethiopia in 1435.  He instead approached his reign with an iron will and determination.  He was a Christian, and arranged a compromise between Egyptian and Ethiopian bishops regarding observation of the Sabbath.  He wrote three significant theological texts while reigning as emperor.  Last, he sent an expedition to Europe that made contact with the Pope and the King of Aragon.
heros.name: Zara Yaqob
